clue.text: A Teletubby's broken into a cattle pen across the pond, officer

indicators.note: something that has broken into a pen has got inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.words: a cattle pen across the pond
parts.note: a corral is the American word for a cattle enclosure; across the pond means in the USA
Po is one of the four Teletubbies of the children's TV show

explanation.surface: A children's TV character has escaped into an American stockyard, and an officer is involved.
explanation.walkthrough: The Teletubbies are characters from a British children's TV show; the red one is Po.
explanation.definitionFit: A corporal is a junior non-commissioned officer in the army.

clue.text: Balls featuring in quotes regularly

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, here every second one of the words in quotes

explanation.surface: Balls keep turning up among things people say, every so often.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: both words are vulgar terms for testicles and also mean nonsense.

clue.text: Countess Olivia and Malvolio, easily deceived? Yes at first, in Twelfth Night perhaps

indicators.note: says to take the opening letter of each of the words before it

explanation.surface: Characters from Shakespeare's play: Olivia the countess and her steward Malvolio, gulled by a forged letter.
explanation.walkthrough: In Twelfth Night Malvolio is tricked into believing Countess Olivia loves him, so the surface is drawn from the play itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Shakespeare's Twelfth Night is one of his best-known comic plays.

clue.text: Extremely evasive during affair? That makes sense

indicators.note: one thing happening during another sits within it, so these letters go inside

parts.note: a fling is a brief love affair

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone being dodgy about a love affair, which is apparently understandable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That makes' is a link to the definition 'sense'; the whole phrase 'That makes sense' reads like an aside.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: touch, or a sense of something, is called a feeling.

clue.text: Tall, thin person with a pulse to measure

parts.note: a bean is a pulse, an edible seed of the pea family
a pole is an old unit of length, five and a half yards

explanation.surface: Taking the pulse of a tall, skinny patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' suggests a heartbeat but means an edible legume here; a pole is an old British measure of length.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal term: a lanky, skinny person is jokingly compared to a stick for climbing plants.

clue.text: Frenchman in Italy playing in Open with all the relatives there?

indicators.note: the Frenchman-in-Italy group is placed in the word for open

parts.note: free means open, unrestricted

indicators.note: the Frenchman goes in the jumbled letters of Italy
letters that are playing about are moving around into a new order

parts.note: M is the abbreviation of Monsieur, a Frenchman

explanation.surface: A Frenchman in Italy plays in a tournament with his whole family watching.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue uses 'in' twice: the first puts M among the shuffled letters, making AMILYT, and the second puts that group inside the word for open.
explanation.definitionFit: A genealogical chart shows every relative of a family, so they are all there on it.

clue.text: Asian people in the old capital of India

parts.note: ye is an archaic spelling of the
men are people

indicators.note: a word's capital is its first letter

explanation.surface: An Asian population living in India's former capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Yemen, a country of south-west Asia, is a native of that nation.

clue.text: Like Knotty Ash's hooter, keeping awfully loud

indicators.note: one thing keeping another holds it within

parts.note: a hooter is slang for a nose

indicators.note: done awfully means done badly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Knotty Ash, the Liverpool suburb made famous by comedian Ken Dodd, and its nose kept very noisy.
explanation.walkthrough: Knotty Ash is a district of Liverpool; the definition is just 'Like Knotty', and 'Ash's hooter' is the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanical adjective: something with many knobs or nodules is described as knotty.

clue.text: Very happy heading off behind schedule

indicators.note: with its head taken off, the first letter goes

parts.note: belated means late, behind schedule

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled to be setting off, even though running late.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: being overjoyed or thrilled is being very happy.

clue.text: Copies from a month back

indicators.note: going back means reading the month's abbreviation from right to left

parts.note: Sep is short for September

explanation.surface: Copies made from something a month ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to ape someone is to imitate or copy them.

clue.text: Teasing Len about bloomers

indicators.note: the letters are moved about into a different order

explanation.surface: Someone teasing a man named Len about his old-fashioned knickers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomers' looks like underwear but means flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the sweet briar, a wild rose, flowers, so it is literally something that blooms.

clue.text: Sort of flat cap on chimneypot

definitions.meaning: a ... flat is a self-contained annexe for an elderly relative
a revolving cowl fitted on top of a chimney to improve the draught

explanation.surface: A rooftop scene: a flat and a cover on its chimney.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a granny flat is a small annexe, and a granny is a chimney cowl.

clue.text: 3 by 17, after 4 it's time for a song!

definitions.text: 3 by 17, after 4 it's time for a song!

parts.words: 3 by 17, after 4 it's time for a song!
parts.note: the clue points to a 1980 comic film, to working office hours, and to a hit song by Dolly Parton of the same name

explanation.walkthrough: 3 is COMEDY, 17 is REDRAFT and 4 is FEELING; the film became a stage musical, a reworking of the comedy, and a song.
explanation.definitionFit: Several senses: the standard office working day, the Jane Fonda and Dolly Parton comedy film, and Parton's theme song.

clue.text: Antibiotic, one dispensed by my chemist if necessary initially

indicators.note: dispensing medicine suggests mixing it up, so the letters are rearranged
take the first letter of each of these words

explanation.surface: A pharmacist hands out an antibiotic only when it is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is an antibiotic drug used chiefly on the skin and in the gut.

clue.text: Black line below boob

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
under means below

explanation.surface: A dark line drawn under a breast, as a cosmetic or medical marking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boob' suggests a breast but here means a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: a boob is a silly error or gaffe.

clue.text: Paradoxically, odds on good service

parts.note: evens is a betting price, so odds that are evens is the paradox of odd being even

explanation.surface: A gambler's tip that the odds favour a good outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an evening church service in the Anglican tradition.

clue.text: Float east of Bordeaux, say, to 22A again

indicators.note: in an across entry, east of something means to its right, so after it

parts.note: Bordeaux is an example of a red wine
a raft is a float

explanation.surface: Drifting east of the French city Bordeaux.
explanation.walkthrough: 22A is SKETCH, so the definition reads 'to sketch again'.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw up a second version of an outline is to make a fresh draft of it.

clue.text: Confront first of medics and demand something to stop germs spreading

parts.note: to face is to confront

indicators.note: take only the opening letter of the word

parts.note: ask means demand

explanation.surface: Taking doctors to task and insisting on infection control.
explanation.definitionFit: Covering the nose and mouth with cloth or paper limits the spread of infection.

clue.text: After trip to China, a tonic's drunk at hotel — ah, our Nina's managed City once

indicators.note: drunk describes letters that are reeling, so they are mixed up

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A traveller back from China drinks a tonic at the hotel and remarks on the setter's hidden message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After trip to China' and 'ah, our Nina's managed' are surface padding: the setter's aside that the puzzle's hidden message (its Nina) has been fitted in.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Syrian city, now Antakya in Turkey, was a great city of the classical world.

clue.text: Temple of Hope, Nantes, mostly rebuilt

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put together in a new arrangement
most of each word is used, so the last letter of each goes

explanation.surface: A church of Hope in the French city of Nantes being largely reconstructed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims both words, giving HOP and NANTE, which 'rebuilt' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Pantheon in Rome was built as a temple to all the gods.

clue.text: A cereal's 2

parts.note: corn is a cereal, and the apostrophe s supplies a final S

explanation.walkthrough: 2 refers to the answer of 2 Down, so the definition is that word.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the fruits of the oak are a kind of hard-shelled seed of that type.

clue.text: Outline of small boat

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: The silhouette of a little boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a rough drawing or summary gives the outline of something.

clue.text: Run like a spinster

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a ... is one run scored
a spinster is an unmarried woman, so not married

explanation.surface: An unmarried woman taking flight.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: one run in cricket, and unmarried.

clue.text: Fielders starting to come in soon, since stupid 'bad' declaration?

indicators.note: the letter is placed into the middle of the other letters
stupid suggests something muddled, so these letters are jumbled
the starting letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Cricket captain tells the fielders to come in, after a foolish declaration.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a captain's declaration ends an innings early; here a declaration is an admission of wrongdoing, which is why 'bad' sits in quotes.
explanation.definitionFit: An admission of wrongdoing is a declaration of something bad you have done.

clue.text: Jogger, handsome, moving house

indicators.note: the words house, or contain, the answer within them

explanation.surface: A handsome jogger is relocating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jogger' is not a runner but a memory jogger.
explanation.definitionFit: A short written reminder jogs the memory.

clue.text: Chap put in order worth £333.33?

definitions.meaning: a man who belongs to a religious order
a monkey is British slang for 500 pounds; the first four of its six letters are two thirds of it, worth two thirds of 500

explanation.surface: A man tidied up, and a question of what he is worth.
explanation.walkthrough: MONKEY is slang for £500; MONK is its first two thirds, so it is playfully 'worth' £333.33.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother of a religious community lives under its rule, so belongs to an order.

clue.text: A French girl with new flat? On the contrary

parts.note: un is the French for a (masculine)
Eve is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A French girl moves into a new flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat? On the contrary' means the opposite of flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonym: a surface that is not level is bumpy or irregular.

clue.text: Settle in: for starters, it's snug enough

parts.note: the printed punctuation mark is a colon

indicators.note: take the first letter of each word that follows

explanation.surface: Making yourself at home: for a start, the place is cosy enough.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon after 'Settle in' is part of the wordplay, giving its own name.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle in a new land, establishing a community there, is to make it a colony.
